# EventConductor

> Event-driven workflow / saga orchestration engine for Java/Spring. Describe a business process as a workflow definition (JSON or YAML) made of steps; the engine drives the state machine and delegates business logic to stateless workers. Scales from a single in-process JVM (no Kafka, no DB) to a multi-pod Kubernetes cluster (Kafka + PostgreSQL) with no change to business code.

EventConductor covers the full lifecycle of a business process — definition, execution, and monitoring — without BPMN's complexity or a SaaS dependency. Two independent properties select the deployment topology: `workflow.mode` (`embedded` | `kafka`, default `embedded`) and `workflow.persistence` (`memory` | `jpa`, default `memory`). Start fully embedded and grow into JPA and then Kafka as scale demands. Artifacts are published to Maven Central under `io.mateu.workflow` (`workflow-engine`, `forms-engine`, `rule-engine`, `rule-runtime`).

## AI reference files

For AI-assisted development, use these context documents with your AI tool (Claude Projects, Cursor Rules, Gemini Gems, etc.):

- [Compact reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/eventconductor/main/doc/public/eventconductor-ai-compact.md): key concepts, the workflow DSL, step types, worker API, statuses. Use for day-to-day code generation.
- [Full reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/eventconductor/main/doc/public/eventconductor-ai-full.md): complete DSL, deployment modes, Kafka topics, full Java API, sagas, git-import, forms, MCP. Use for thorough assistance.
- Claude Code / Claude Agent SDK: bundled skills at `.claude/skills/eventconductor*/` auto-activate for EventConductor tasks (define workflows, implement workers, scaffold, run).
- [Workflow definition JSON Schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/miguelperezcolom/eventconductor/main/modules/workflow-engine/src/main/resources/workflow-definition-schema.json): for editor autocomplete and validation of `.json`/`.yaml` definitions.

## Key concepts

- A **workflow definition** (`id`, `name`, `version`, `status`, `steps`) is JSON or YAML; in embedded/memory mode it is loaded from `classpath:/workflows/`.
- Steps run **by pure data flow**: a step starts when **all** its preconditions (`preconditionStepIds`, or the singular `preconditionStepId`) have completed and its JEXL guard holds — not by array order. All eligible steps start concurrently; the `parallel` flag is deprecated and ignored. Every step with no preconditions must be a `START` or a `WAIT_FOR_MESSAGE` (the entry points) — definitions violating this are rejected at load.
- **Step types**: `START` (entry point; no worker, completes instantly at process creation; several = concurrent entry branches), `ACTION` (dispatch to a worker via `topic`), `USER_TASK` (human form via `formId`), `RULE` (evaluate a business rule via `ruleId`; outputs become process variables), `TIMER` (durable wait for an ISO 8601 `duration` or until a date in `untilVariable`), `WAIT_FOR_MESSAGE` (wait for a message via `messageName`, correlated by the required JEXL `correlationExpression` — use `businessKey` to correlate by business key), `SEND_MESSAGE` (fire-and-forget: emit a message with `messageName`, the key from `correlationExpression` and the process variables named in `messageVariables`), `PROCESS` (child workflow via `childWorkflowDefinitionId`; parent step waits for the child and copies back the child variables named in `outputVariables`), `FORK` (explicit fan-out; completes instantly, all successors start concurrently), `JOIN` (barrier; its `preconditionStepIds` must all complete), `END` (recommended one per workflow; JOIN before it if branches exist).
- **Variables** are `(name, value)` string pairs; worker outputs are merged into process variables and available to later steps and to JEXL `preconditionExpression`s.
- **Workers** are stateless: they receive a `TaskExecutionRequested` and report `RUNNING` | `COMPLETED` | `ERROR` with output variables. Report using `taskExecutionId`, not the workflow `stepId`.
- **Embedded mode**: register one `EmbeddedTaskExecutor` bean (or per-`topic` beans) and inject `UpdateStepExecutionUseCase`. **Kafka mode**: consume `downstream`, publish `TaskStatusChanged` to `upstream`.
- Start a process with `ProcessUpstreamEventUseCase.handle(new ProcessUpstreamEventCommand(new ProcessCreationRequested(workflowId, businessKey, variables)))`, or send `ProcessCreationRequested` to the `upstream` Kafka topic.
- **Retries & timeouts**: `retries: N` and `timeout` (ISO-8601 `PT30S` or ms) on a step. **Saga**: `rollbackable: true` + `compensationStepId` run a compensation step on failure.
- **Pause/resume**: `PauseProcessUseCase`/`ResumeProcessUseCase` freeze a process (`PAUSED` status): in-flight work still finishes and messages are accepted, but successors are held and timer/timeout clocks freeze (shifted forward by the pause duration on resume). `PauseWorkflowUseCase`/`ResumeWorkflowUseCase` pause a whole definition (`paused` flag): new instances — cron included — are still created, born paused. Also in the UI and as MCP tools (`pauseProcess`/`resumeProcess`/`pauseWorkflow`/`resumeWorkflow`).
- **Deployment** is two properties (`workflow.mode`, `workflow.persistence`); the same business code runs from a single JVM to a Kafka+PostgreSQL cluster.
- **Business rules**: `rule-engine` is the catalog (JSON/YAML definitions, `expression` rules and `decision-table`s validated against a schema, git-import, UI, MCP tools, REST + gRPC read APIs); `rule-runtime` is the lightweight embeddable evaluator (JEXL). `rules.source` selects where the runtime reads rules from: `local` (same JVM), `classpath`, `rest` or `grpc`, with a TTL cache and optional Kafka refresh (`RulePublished`/`RuleDeleted` on the `rules` topic).
